propositions: Three separate verifier code paths (verify.py, completion.py, code-review.yaml) independently select the model by comparing cfg.model against DEFAULT_MODEL or falling through to cfg.model directly, causing downgrades to fail when models are provider-qualified (e.g., 'anthropic:claude-opus-4-8' != 'claude-opus-4-8').

Code-review's Pass-2 verify step declares temperature: 0 for determinism but runs on the frontier model because the step has no model: key; moving it to standard class makes the temperature setting effective and downgrades to the default provider.

All three verifier paths must resolve the reserved class names (standard/trivial/frontier) through a single resolve_model_string() function in model_classes.py, with separate call sites in config.resolve_model(), verify.py, plan_review/__init__.py, and completion.py.
resolve_model() in config.py must call resolve_model_string() lazily (function-level import) to avoid a circular import, since model_classes already imports from config at module scope.

With Bedrock configured as the standard class provider, no verifier path should resolve a model from a different provider (anthropic direct); existing code leaks the frontier model from provider-qualified ids that fail equality tests.

A workflow YAML step whose model: field is a literal model id must resolve to that id unchanged for backward compatibility; only the reserved strings (standard/trivial/frontier) trigger class resolution.
